title: M-House / Country House. Architecture
text:
M-House / Country House. Architecture

Amid a quiet neighborhood in Phan Thiet, where the sun warms the walls and sea breezes weave their way beneath tiled roofs, M-House emerges with an understated charm. On a modest plot surrounded by neighboring homes on three sides, we chose an open architectural configuration to bring natural light, fresh air, and greenery into everyday life.

title: Casa Amigó / Estudio Travertino
text:
Casa Amigó / Estudio Travertino

Some renovations update spaces; others reorganize how they are lived in. Casa Amigó belongs to the second group. Located in Barcelona's Sant Gervasi-Galvany neighborhood, this 1970s family home starts with a clear idea: to change how the space is perceived and inhabited. The project turns the flat into an interior landscape where color, material, and light reorganize the relationships between rooms.

title: Rosaleda Terrace / RH-EL
text:
Rosaleda Terrace / RH-EL

Behind a discreet fence in a residence located in Villahermosa city of Tabasco. You can find a majestic garden hidden. The property has the fortune to be situated on the shores of the iconic Illusions Lagoon, where you can see part of Tabasco’s faun, like morelet’s crocodiles, pejelagartos, manatees and some birds from the region.

title: Sede Ser Headquarters / Atelier 77
text:
Sede Ser Headquarters / Atelier 77

The expansion of the Ser Cidadão Headquarters in Santa Cruz, the west zone of Rio de Janeiro, embodies in architecture the commitment of a social organization to human and community development. Since 2002, the organization has been involved in projects related to education, culture, work, and health, promoting opportunities for youth in vulnerable territories. In 2006, it received a donation of a historic mansion, the former residence of doctor and senator Júlio Cesário de Melo, whose legacy of care inspired the very essence of the project: to build spaces that welcome, educate, and transform.

title: LDN House / ERENTIA
text:
LDN House / ERENTIA

In LDN, ERENTIA transforms an existing London residence into a home for two: two people who share a life, but not necessarily all of their daily needs. The project rethinks domestic structure through varying degrees of proximity, creating spaces that allow the couple to gather, share, and find distance when needed. Two people, one house, two workspaces. One bathroom, two sinks, two showers. Autonomy, parallels, and distance.

title: AUA Najarian Center / Storaket Architectural Studio
text:
AUA Najarian Center / Storaket Architectural Studio

The Najarian Center is a key facility of the American University of Armenia (AUA), located in Yerevan, near the Sergei Parajanov Museum. Established with the support of K. George and Dr. Carolann Najarian, the center is part of a broader initiative to drive social change in Armenia through education and innovation. It provides spaces and resources for learning, collaboration, and fostering social entrepreneurship. As part of the project, reconstruction work has been carried out on the building, including seismic retrofitting, interior and exterior renovations, and the comprehensive implementation of engineering systems.

title: Modern and Mexican: Mario Pani’s CUPA Housing Complex in Mexico City
text:
Modern and Mexican: Mario Pani’s CUPA Housing Complex in Mexico City

In 1947, Mexico's General Directorate of Civil Pensions commissioned young architect Mario Pani to design 200 houses for government employees on a recently acquired plot of land in Colonia del Valle, then a distant neighborhood on the outskirts of Mexico City. Rather than following the original guidelines, Pani proposed a 13-story housing complex with extensive green areas, communal spaces, and more than a thousand apartments. Drawing on Le Corbusier's functionalist principles, the architect created a project that opened in 1949 and would become a landmark in Latin American modern architecture.

title: ATO RAMEN / CUDO:
text:
ATO RAMEN / CUDO:

The starting point for ATO Ramen in Warsaw was the idea of making the ramen-making process an essential part of the guest experience. Rather than hiding food preparation behind closed doors, we designed an open kitchen and a glazed noodle production area as the heart of the restaurant.

title: Strata House / VPA Architects
text:
Strata House / VPA Architects

Strata House is a project rooted in quiet and calming living. The house was curated around a singular conviction — designing around the climate to make light and shadows its most eloquent architectural gesture. The south-facing plot demanded a pronounced response. Deep overhead projections extend across the façade to intercept the sun before it reaches the open glass beneath. The built mass stretches further towards the west to cast shade over the garden and veranda below, extending the architecture itself into a landscape of comfort. These sleek floating slabs are functional at their core, yet visually, they give the elevation a unique identity: a composition of strong horizontals and quiet repose. On the exterior, a locally quarried and fine-grained Gwalior Mint sandstone wraps the building with a characteristic green-grey luminosity, carrying the memory of its region with a material honesty.

title: Police Station for the People / STUDIO MOTLEY
text:
Police Station for the People / STUDIO MOTLEY

"Build us a Police Station that people don't find intimidating." This simple, yet unusually perceptive brief from the Additional Commissioner became the starting point for rethinking the conventional police station. Located in Devanahalli, a town on the outskirts of Bangalore with a history spanning over 500 years, the project offered an opportunity to reconsider not just the architecture of a largely neglected building typology, but also the relationship between a public institution and the people it serves.

title: Biarritz Building - Cooperative Housing / Ariel Jacubovich | Oficina de Arquitectura
text:
Biarritz Building - Cooperative Housing / Ariel Jacubovich | Oficina de Arquitectura

Biarritz is a 35-unit residential building in the district of San Martín, Province of Buenos Aires, developed alongside a cooperative of teachers and education workers. It is the result of a participatory process initiated in 2017 that spanned from searching for the land to the actual construction, including training workshops, debates on ways of living, and even policy proposals for democratic housing development created in collaboration with local organizations.

title: Aquatics Centre Paris / VenhoevenCS + Ateliers 2/3/4/
text:
Aquatics Centre Paris / VenhoevenCS + Ateliers 2/3/4/

The Aquatics Centre and its pedestrian overpass in Saint-Denis, Paris, designed by VenhoevenCS and Ateliers 2/3/4/ for Heritage, is the only permanent facility built for the 2024 Games. The Aquatics Centre emerges as a curved wooden sculpture from the Grand Paris landscape, combining technical innovations with the highest environmental credentials. With its clever configuration, limited need of materials and energy under an ultra-thin hanging roof, France's largest urban solar farm, the arena will host 5.000 spectators for water polo, diving and artistic swimming Olympic competitions.

title: House AL / N2B Arquitetura
text:
House AL / N2B Arquitetura

Located in the Vila do Golf area, House AL was designed to take advantage of the terrain's slope. Divided into three levels, the residence offers privileged views of the landscape, both above and below the treetops, integrating its outdoor area, situated on the lower level, with the local scenery.

title: Ca la Tecla Renovation / Hiha Studio
text:
Ca la Tecla Renovation / Hiha Studio

Records show that the building has existed since 1572. Over the centuries, the property has been occupied by different generations and family units, undergoing various transformations and adaptations to meet the needs of each period.

title: Lamberth Palace Arches / Tigg + Coll Architects
text:
Lamberth Palace Arches / Tigg + Coll Architects

TiggColl has transformed three previously underutilised Victorian railway arches beneath one of London's busiest railway routes into new spaces for studying, socialising and relaxing, developing a demountable mass-timber system that responds to the unique technical challenges of working beneath an active railway.

title: Mapping Memory: Reconstructing Architecture Beyond Physical Evidence
text:
Mapping Memory: Reconstructing Architecture Beyond Physical Evidence

How do you remember the dimensions of a room you could barely see? Perhaps through the distance between footsteps, the sound of a door closing, or the way an echo travels down a corridor. For someone who has been denied the ability to see or move freely through a space, these fragments may be the only record of its architecture.

title: FLEISCHEREI, A RESTAURANT REWORKED / Allen Kaufmann Architekten
text:
FLEISCHEREI, A RESTAURANT REWORKED / Allen Kaufmann Architekten

Fleischerei carries the traces of a 1911 building, a former butcher shop and the restaurant that opened there in 2009, while being reworked for a new life in 2025 and 2026.

title: Exhibition Artifact / Configuración Visual
text:
Exhibition Artifact / Configuración Visual

The Exhibition Artifact (Artefacto Expositivo) arose from a commission to build a temporary support to exhibit architectural models developed by students of the UNIACC School of Architecture during a celebration of the academic community. In response to this brief, the project proposes to expand the possibilities of the exhibition display, understanding that a structure designed to hold objects can, at the same time, create an environment capable of hosting a collective gathering.

title: House Duas Marias I / Canoa Arquitetura
text:
House Duas Marias I / Canoa Arquitetura

House Duas Marias I is located in Jaguariúna, in the countryside of São Paulo state. It was built on a plot of approximately 6,000 m², which already featured large mature trees, especially in its lower section.

title: Hotel Tepoztlán / Taller Carlos Marín + Pasquinel Studio
text:
Hotel Tepoztlán / Taller Carlos Marín + Pasquinel Studio

Located between Tepoztlán and Amatlán in the State of Morelos, the Hotel Tepoztlpán designed by the Carlos Marín and Pasquinel Studio Workshop Offices integrates the topography, the landscape and the views of the Tepozteco in a master plan where 4 buildings with different architectural programs explore the virtues of the site. The land was an abandoned plot, where wild vegetation, along with several medium and tall trees were located naturally on the site. From the beginning, this natural condition and respect for the flora of the site was a determining factor for positioning each of the volumes that comprise the project. Another condition that the terrain presents is its rugged topography, the access volume -a staple of pigmented concrete- is located at the foot of the sidewalk, and as we go deeper into the terrain we discover the 4 buildings, the terrain dictated the terrain and program of each of the buildings. The gentle ramps and staircases allow us to reach the pool area, which is -2.5m from the access level, while the room building makes the first forced stop for the user to the center of the land and to an altitude of - 1.20m.

title: Canal Beach Nature Resort / Atelier Bugio
text:
Canal Beach Nature Resort / Atelier Bugio

The property, located in the Southwest Alentejo and Vicentina Coast Natural Park, features three main areas: a higher ridge area, a plateau area, and an extensive valley oriented northwest, extending all the way to the sea. The intervention stems from a thorough analysis of the territory with the aim of establishing a strong relationship with it, incorporating it without altering it. It is governed by a fundamental premise: to align the experience of the surrounding natural environment with the very experience of staying in the hotel.

title: Darwin Bridges / Provencher_Roy
text:
Darwin Bridges / Provencher_Roy

Located on Nuns' Island in Montréal, the Darwin bridges open new architectural perspectives through their use of local sustainable materials.

title: Hotel Casa Zamná Tulum / Studio Arquitectos
text:
Hotel Casa Zamná Tulum / Studio Arquitectos

Located on the heavenly beaches of Tulum, Casa Zamná is an architectural project facing the Caribbean Sea. This boutique hotel developed on a 5,160 m² plot and carefully designed by StudioArqs, stands as a tribute to nature and local culture, achieving a harmonious fusion between contemporary design and the most traditional elements of the region.

title: Snake Building / C+S Architects
text:
Snake Building / C+S Architects

The Snake Building in Aarschot, Belgium, is part of a collaboration with a2o Architekten, a Hasselt-based office, commissioned by the client to design the urban regeneration of the De Torens masterplan: a former industrial site in the center of Aarschot, developed with housing, commercial, and public spaces. A series of collegial workshops in Hasselt initiated the design process and assigned the plots to each office (a2o Architekten, C+S Architects, De Vylder Vynck and DRDH).
